acceptance: On timeout, adapters that can do so cancel the statement and stop the session this run started, shown with stubbed clients.
A warning tells cloud users that remote work may continue and that cleanup is not live-verified.
The per-adapter capability table is in the pull request.
description:
## Problem
When BenchBox stops at a timeout, a query, job or session it started on a remote platform can keep running and billing. Read on develop: only GizmoSQL cancels a running query (`adbc_cancel`); Onehouse has `cancel_job` (onehouse/onehouse_client.py:330) that nothing calls; no other adapter calls a cancel API.

## Owner decision
"build the remote cleanup, verify it with stubbed clients only, and print a warning on cloud platforms that remote work may continue after a timeout until a live check has been done. No live cloud runs." Source: owner's answer in the choice dialog, 2026-11-20.

## Change
First list every adapter under benchbox/platforms that starts remote work, and what its client offers to cancel a statement and to stop a session, job or cluster BenchBox itself started; put the table in the pull request. Add one adapter hook that the timeout path calls, implemented where the client supports it (Onehouse `cancel_job` at least). Only stop what this run started; never stop a warehouse, cluster or session that existed before the run. Print the warning for every cloud platform when a run limit is set, saying whether cleanup is implemented for that platform. Adapter SDK imports stay lazy.

## Decision gates
A limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has chosen is used verbatim (see run-timeout-plan-20261120). Any other new name or message follows existing BenchBox conventions and is listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop for these). The warning uses the owner's texts verbatim (2026-11-21). Cleanup implemented: "A run time limit is set. If the run times out, BenchBox will try to cancel the work it started on {platform}. This cleanup has not been checked against the live service, so work may keep running and billing." Not implemented: "A run time limit is set. If the run times out, work BenchBox started on {platform} may keep running and billing: BenchBox cannot cancel it on this platform." No live cloud run, no credentials used. Verification is by stubbed clients, and the docs and the warning say cleanup has not been checked against live services. If an adapter cannot tell what it started from what pre-existed, it implements no cleanup and the table says so.

## Verification rubric
Pass, each by a test that fails before the change: per adapter with cleanup, a stubbed client shows the cancel and stop calls are made on timeout for resources the run started and not for pre-existing ones; the hook is called from the timeout path, including the backstop path, and a failing cleanup does not hide the timeout (exit code stays 124, the cleanup error is reported); the warning appears for cloud platforms when a limit is set and not otherwise, and not for local platforms; the docs carry the same statement. `make platform-manifest-check` and `make pr-preflight` exit 0.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking; `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job that never ran or was cancelled by the runner, never for a test that failed. Review threads: reply, and resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again. Subagents implement batch members and serial items under the delivery plan on run-timeout-plan-20261120 (owner, 2026-11-21); a batch member makes no tracker write, opens no pull request and stops at a landing report. A limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has chosen is used verbatim (see run-timeout-plan-20261120). Any other new name or message follows existing BenchBox conventions and is listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop for these). No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment. A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`.
